clue.text: Starts to corner in reverse, copper goes to second round junction

indicators.note: the starts of the next three words are their opening letters, taken in turn

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Driving instructions: turn backwards at a corner, the policeman heading for the second roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but gives the chemical symbol. A circus in British place names (Oxford Circus, Piccadilly Circus) is a round open space where streets meet.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a circus is a circular junction of streets, as at Oxford Circus in London.

clue.text: Player with only one leg

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
pod is the Greek root for foot or leg, as in tripod, a stand on three legs

explanation.surface: A footballer or athlete who has only a single leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests a sportsman; it is a music player. A tripod has three legs, so the jokey one-legged version is I (one) plus POD.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple's portable device is a well-known music player.

clue.text: It's in most papers: "Former BBC chat show host Jonathan breaks its ultimate taboo"

indicators.note: one word breaking another splits it open and sits in the gap

parts.note: the C-word is reckoned the most taboo word in English

parts.words: Former BBC chat show host Jonathan
parts.note: Jonathan Ross hosted a long-running BBC chat show

explanation.surface: A newspaper quotes a chat-show host who has said the unsayable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks' signals the container. Jonathan Ross is a British TV presenter who left the BBC after a 2008 scandal; the C-word is a swear word too rude to print.
explanation.definitionFit: Most daily newspapers carry a puzzle grid of this kind, as this one does.

clue.text: More than one episode of hospital drama that's featured in top and bottom of schedules

indicators.note: featuring in something means sitting inside it
the top and bottom of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: ER is the long-running US hospital drama
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A TV listing note says a hospital drama leads and closes the evening's schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A run of episodes of a programme is a series.

clue.text: Part company in Spain after standard within Spanish car maker

indicators.note: Spain's letter comes after the rest in the answer
one piece placed within another is put inside it

parts.note: SEAT is the Spanish car manufacturer
par is the standard, as in up to par
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A business split up in Spain, following a standards dispute at a carmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Within' puts the standard inside the carmaker; 'after' puts Spain's letter at the end. E is the international car code for Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate is to part company, going separate ways.

clue.text: Opening up isn't categorised in instructions for theatre

indicators.note: opening up a word breaks it open so its letters can be arranged afresh

parts.note: letters taken as written; the apostrophe is ignored

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a newly opened show refuses to be pigeonholed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening up' signals the anagram of ISNTCATEGORISED, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Directions printed in a script tell actors where to move and how, guiding the staging.

clue.text: This beats Paul's cryptic rubbish standing on its head!

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of Paul's, with the S

indicators.note: in a down clue a word upside down reads from bottom to top

parts.note: rot means rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: A fellow setter is mocked: Paul's cryptics are nonsense turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: PAULS is rearranged to PULSA; 'standing on its head' turns ROT to TOR. Paul is a fellow Guardian setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that pulses or throbs regularly is a pulsator: it beats.

clue.text: Bird of prey

definitions.meaning: an old word for plunder or prey, also spelt ravin, and as a verb to seize prey

explanation.definitionFit: The bird is the big black crow; the archaic noun means plunder or prey.

clue.text: Left loo with litter scattered, something pointed out in hotel bathroom

definitions.text: something pointed out in hotel bathroom

indicators.note: scattered items are strewn about, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a hotel lavatory with rubbish strewn across the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of L plus LOO plus LITTER; 'with' is a joining word. Hotels often fold the loose end into a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotel housekeepers fold the end sheet of the paper roll into a neat point.

clue.text: Where bars prohibit entry?

parts.note: bars read as barriers barring access, while the surface suggests pubs refusing customers

explanation.surface: A pub-goer wonders where bars turn people away.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone people are barred from entering is a forbidden area.

clue.text: Player that's affected can be seen by all — two characters when touching might represent women in story

indicators.note: the pieces go in the story word, inside it

parts.note: a lie is a story, a falsehood
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

parts.words: two characters when touching might represent women
parts.note: two letter Vs side by side look like W, the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: An affected actor shows himself to all, playing two characters who represent women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts the letters inside the story. U is the British film rating meaning suitable for everyone, and two Vs together look like a W.
explanation.definitionFit: A luvvie is a gushing, theatrical actor, a player with affectations.

clue.text: Part of play, playwright clutching opening to act — he covers the background in theatre

definitions.text: he covers the background in theatre

parts.note: a scene is a division of a play

indicators.note: one piece clutching another holds it inside

parts.note: Harold Pinter was a British playwright

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A theatre programme describes a playwright who grabs the start of an act.
explanation.walkthrough: PINTER clutches A (opening to 'act') to give PAINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenery artist paints the backdrops behind the actors on stage.

clue.text: Single? God, in this, mum loses right to carry on being married

indicators.note: carrying something holds it inside
losing a letter drops it from the word

parts.note: mum means mother
is means exists, being

explanation.surface: A single mother loses her right to remain married, and asks whether God is in this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loses' drops R from mum, giving MOTHE; 'to carry' puts ON inside it. 'Single' looks like an unmarried mother but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief in only one deity, the single god of this creed.

clue.text: Where you might see a car boot sale with free parking?

definitions.text: Where you might see a car boot sale with free parking?

parts.words: Where you might see a car boot sale with free parking?
parts.note: a car and a boot are playing pieces, property is sold, and Free Parking is a square, all on a board game

explanation.surface: A shopper asks where a car boot sale with free parking could be found.
explanation.walkthrough: A car boot sale is a British flea market where people sell from their car boots (trunks); here the car and boot are game tokens.
explanation.definitionFit: The property-trading board game has car and boot tokens and a Free Parking square.

clue.text: Latin line following wedding vow of excessive devotion

indicators.note: Latin and line come after the vow in the answer

parts.note: I do is said at a wedding
Ry is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A Latin line follows the wedding vow, expressing extreme devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is worship of idols, and so any extravagant devotion.

clue.text: Now begrudge supporting group of professional racketeers

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits below the other

parts.note: the ATP is the Association of Tennis Professionals, players wielding rackets
to resent is to begrudge

explanation.surface: A grudge holder backs a gang of professional crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racketeers' suggests gangsters but means tennis players with rackets.
explanation.definitionFit: At present means currently, now.

clue.text: Makes a pig of final parts to George Gershwin song, stripping Porgy and Bess

indicators.note: the final parts of words are their last letters
stripping a word removes its outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: Someone takes the end of a Gershwin song and strips the leads from Porgy and Bess.
explanation.walkthrough: Last letters E, N, G; Porgy and Bess stripped give ORG and ES.
explanation.definitionFit: To engorge is to gorge oneself, stuffing like a pig.

clue.text: Reduce Tory 26

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, a Tory
the answer to 26 across means thick, and dense is thick

explanation.surface: A remark that a Tory is the dimwit of the clue at 26.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 across is OBTUSE, meaning thick, which gives DENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense is to reduce, making shorter or more concentrated.

clue.text: See 13
Small restaurant covering Ramsay's starter with gravy

indicators.note: one piece covering another surrounds it

parts.note: Bisto is a well-known British gravy brand

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Gordon Ramsay's starter arrives smothered in gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: BISTO covers R. Bisto is a British gravy powder; Gordon Ramsay is a celebrity chef.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small informal restaurant.

clue.text: Must've?

parts.note: think gives MUSE, which sits outside TV, the box, spelling the clue word

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: a word for think (MUSE) placed outside the box (TV), giving MUSTVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To think creatively in new ways is a must for solvers of this clue.

clue.text: Sound of horse that's not far away taking Aintree's last

indicators.note: taking something in holds it inside

parts.note: nigh means near, not far away

indicators.note: the last letter of a word is its final one

explanation.surface: A horse whinnies near the finish at Aintree.
explanation.walkthrough: NIGH takes in E. Aintree is the course of the Grand National horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the high whinnying cry of a horse.

clue.text: Thieves empty bank?

definitions.meaning: emptying a bank is what a raider does to it

explanation.definitionFit: To rob is to thieve from someone, and a raid empties a bank.

clue.text: Heartless shooting — nail-biting alternative?

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: shooting a film is filming

explanation.surface: A heartless shooting is described as an alternative to nail-biting tension.
explanation.walkthrough: FILMING loses its heart, M. 'Nail-biting' suggests tension; it is a nail habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Filing your nails tidies them instead of biting them.

clue.text: See 20
Some Conservative MP has isolated stress

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Tory MP has cut himself off, and is under stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis means stress laid on a word or point.

clue.text: Thick fat — needs heart replacing by Tuesday

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, here swapped for another piece

parts.note: obese means very fat

explanation.surface: A fat person needs a heart transplant by Tuesday.
explanation.walkthrough: OBESE's middle E is replaced by TU.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow-witted, thick.
